verified.note: Abstract confirms verbatim: 608 million (95% UI 518-724) females 15+ ever exposed to IPV; 18.5 million (8.74-30.0) DALYs; IPV ranked 4th (SVAC 5th) leading risk factor for DALYs among females 15-49; anxiety disorders 5.43 million and MDD 3.96 million DALYs. relevance_to_tphe correctly hedges that this is a burden estimate, not evidence T-PHE works.

27% (UI 23-31%) lifetime and 13% (10-16%) past-year figures and the 24% (21-28%) for age 15-19 figure are verbatim-correct. But the record states '26% aged 20-24' while the fetched abstract literally reads '26% (23-30%) of women aged 19-24 years' (likely an upstream GBD/abstract typo, but the record must match the source text as fetched). FIX: change '20-24' to '19-24' to match the abstract exactly, or flag the age-band as ambiguous in a footnote.

Abstract confirms aRR 0.54 (0.38-0.79) for lower acceptance of IPV among women, and 0.48 (0.16-1.39) for past-year physical IPV among women -- record correctly reports this CI crosses 1 and does not overclaim significance.

Abstract confirms verbatim: community-level norms explained 70% of effect on women's IPV experience and 95% of effect on men's perpetration; men's reduced suspicion of infidelity explained 22% of perpetration effect.
Abstract confirms US$553,252 total 4-year cost, US$5/person/year, 1,201 cases averted (90% CI 97-2,307), US$460/case averted -- all figures match exactly.
Non-empirical programme-description paper confirmed; abstract supports the summary and the P7 (repairability) relevance framing (explicit revision cycle after 10 years of programme learning).

Key_finding content is supported by the abstract. However, first_author is wrong: the record lists 'Kyegombe N' but PubMed's actual first author for PMID 27682273 is 'Starmann E' (Kyegombe N appears to be a co-author, and is the correct first author on a different SASA! paper, PMID 30613427). FIX the first_author field to Starmann E before citing.
Abstract confirms aRR 0.44 (0.34-0.59) women, aRR 0.54 (0.38-0.75) men, and 'There were no study-related harms' verbatim.

Key_finding says the programme 'was associated with reported shifts...over time' but omits the abstract's explicit caveat that shifts were only 'moderate, but significant,' and that 'these shifts occurred without fully transforming deeply-entrenched beliefs and norms,' which the authors say could constrain longevity of change. Given T-PHE's own epistemic-humility/FAILURE CRITERION framing, this caveat should be added rather than presenting the finding as an unqualified positive shift.
Abstract confirms all four programme components (5-month couples curriculum, 2-year community activism, women's safe spaces, opinion-leader training) and the SASA! fidelity brief guidance verbatim.

Two problems. (1) key_finding omits the actual headline quantitative results reported in the abstract -- 'a significant 61% reduction in odds of reporting experiencing any IPV among women, a 64% reduction among Christians, and a 44% reduction in MFP congregations' -- and instead describes only the study design, which understates what was found; rewrite key_finding to include these effect sizes. The claim that the trial was 'explicitly designed and powered to evaluate norms-shifting mechanisms rather than knowledge/attendance alone' is not stated in the abstract and should be removed or re-sourced. (2) first_author is wrong: record lists 'Muluh N' but PubMed's actual first author is 'Shaw B'. FIX author field.
Abstract confirms significant improvement in knowledge/attitudes and a non-significant improvement in self-efficacy/behaviours verbatim.

Key_finding content (seven CFIR inner-setting constructs and their content) is supported by the abstract. However, first_author is wrong: record lists 'Le V (Archdiocese of Chicago Domestic Violence Outreach study)' but PubMed's actual first author is 'Debinski B'. FIX the first_author field.
Abstract confirms the three cross-context pathways (relationship-skills learning, participatory norms-challenge, economic-empowerment integration) verbatim.

Sample sizes (573 CHWs, 562/564 pre/post, 506 at 17-19mo follow-up) are verbatim-correct. But 'facilitators with more education showed smaller attitude shifts' misstates the abstract: the regression finding is that CHWs with some secondary education (coef -2.15, p<0.01) and >3 years' experience (coef -2.27, p<0.001) were LESS LIKELY to hold inequitable attitudes -- a baseline/associational finding about attitude levels, not a finding about the SIZE of pre/post attitude shift during training. Reword key_finding to avoid implying a dose-response on 'shift magnitude' that the abstract does not report.

Key_finding content (null primary child-development outcome, moderate-to-large secondary effects including IPV victimisation) is well supported and the FAILURE CRITERION framing in relevance_to_tphe is apt. However, first_author is a placeholder '(MTM Kenya trial investigators)' rather than PubMed's actual first author 'Jeong J'. FIX the first_author field.
Confirmed as a study protocol with no outcome data (no Results section in the abstract); record correctly flags 'should not be cited for effectiveness'.

Null-result key_finding (aOR 1.25, 95% CI 0.92-1.70) is verbatim-correct and appropriately characterized as null/non-significant. However, first_author is wrong: record lists 'Dunkle K' but PubMed's actual first author for PMID 32257154 is 'Chatterji S' (Dunkle K is the correct first author for the different Indashyikirwa RCT paper, PMID 33355268 -- the two appear to have been conflated). FIX the first_author field.
Abstract confirms 57% vs 31% bystander intervention rate verbatim, and the listed associated factors are a fair subset of the abstract's fuller list.

Key_finding content (CFIR/EPIS/MRC frameworks; fidelity/acceptability/feasibility most studied; scale/sustainability and survivor-centred practice under-addressed) matches the abstract. However, first_author is a placeholder '(VAW/C implementation science scoping review authors)' rather than PubMed's actual first author 'Falb KL'. FIX the first_author field.

overall_note: All 20 PMIDs resolve on PubMed E-utilities and all titles/years match. Numeric key findings (GBD 608M/18.5M DALYs, Sardinha 27%, SASA! aRRs, Indashyikirwa aRRs, cost figures, null-result ORs) were checked against the fetched abstract text and are accurate to the reported precision in 17/20 records. Two systematic problems recur: (1) first_author metadata is wrong or replaced with a generic placeholder in 6 records (PMID 27682273, 37329160, 37649394, 42556995, 32257154, 40462272) -- most concerning is an apparent conflation between two different Dunkle/Rwanda-related and two different SASA!/Kyegombe-related papers, which must be fixed before citation since misattributed authorship in a public manuscript is a real error, not stylistic. (2) Three records (31686618, 37329160, 40625533) either omit important caveats present in the abstract (31686618's 'shifts did not fully transform entrenched norms'), omit the actual headline quantitative result in favor of a vaguer paraphrase (37329160's 61%/64%/44% reduction figures), or subtly misrepresent what a regression coefficient measured (40625533's 'facilitators with more education showed smaller attitude shifts', which the abstract does not say). No record was found to be fabricated, off-topic, or non-PubMed-indexed; no DROP verdicts were issued. Final counts: KEEP 12, FIX 8, DROP 0.
